steps.do: Before you start: the server needs CALIBER_FEATURE_ARIA=true (Aria and Plans are off by default). In the sidebar open Integrations and click Plans. Paste the canonical sentence from intent.md into Goal, set Autonomy to Stop before each change and press Decompose goal. The planner is rules, not a model: it looks for the words judge and eval dataset / test set.
fill: Create a judge for answer faithfulness and an eval dataset to run it on.
steps.see: The plan opens with the status draft and 2 steps.

steps.do: Read Plan steps. Aria drew Create judge (judge.create) and Create test set (eval_dataset.create), in that order, both pending, each listing the inputs it needs (name, instructions and name). Nothing has run. Compare with expected-plan.json.
steps.see: Two pending steps, no wired inputs between them: each step asks for its own name.

steps.do: Press Approve plan. This records that you accept the plan's shape before any step runs.
steps.see: The status becomes approved and an Execute button appears.

steps.do: Press Execute. Aria reaches judge.create and stops on an Aria needs information form (Provide the required inputs for step 1: Create judge.) because the planner cannot know the judge's name or instructions. Fill it from answer-faithfulness.judge.json and press Continue plan. Because you chose Stop before each change, an Aria needs your approval prompt follows (Approve step 1: Create judge (judge.create)?). Press Approve.
fill: You audit whether an assistant answer is faithful to its evidence. You are given the request {{ inputs }}, the model {{ outputs }}, and the reference {{ expectations }}. Return true ONLY if every factual claim in {{ outputs }} is supported by {{ expectations }} (or by evidence cited in {{ inputs }}), and the answer makes no unsupported commitments. If any claim is unsupported, contradicted, or hallucinated, return false. Judge faithfulness only - not style.
steps.see: The judge step reads done and the plan moves on to the test set step.

steps.do: The next form is Provide the required inputs for step 2: Create test set. Fill name, description and tags from support-faithfulness.dataset.json (the tags are a JSON array), press Continue plan, then Approve the prompt Approve step 2: Create test set (eval_dataset.create)?.
steps.see: The plan reads completed and both steps done.

steps.do: Open Test Sets, search for the name and open the set. It is at v1 with no rows: Aria creates the test set empty. Press Import from file and choose faithfulness-cases.jsonl under Test set file. The page reads 30 rows ready to import.; press Import 30 rows.
steps.see: 30 rows in the list and the version reads v31 (one version per row).

steps.do: Modify the test set, which makes a new version. On the first row press Edit, add a sentence to Expected (JSON object) and press Save. Then set Version view to Active as of version and pick 31.
steps.see: The version reads v32 and the row shows the new text; the Active as of version 31 view lists the 30 rows as they were, read-only, without it.

steps.do: Press Run evaluation, pick the test set at v32, give it a Label, untick Exact match, Token F1 and Contains expected, tick Non-empty and, under Custom LLM judges, the judge Aria created. Press Run.
steps.see: On the simulated stack the red message evaluation requires a real LLM provider (nothing is stored). On a stack with a real provider the run scores the 30 rows with the judge; the README's real-provider section versions a prompt (careless v1, grounded v2), runs both and compares them.

steps.do: State a sentence with none of the domain words: Write me a poem about customer support. and press Decompose goal.
steps.see: An amber note, No platform steps matched this goal, so there is nothing to approve.; the sentence stays in the box and no plan opens, so there is nothing to approve (over the API the plan is created with a warning and approve answers 409).
steps.asset: Warning for a sentence with no steps

steps.do: State Create a judge for tone., press Decompose goal, Approve plan, Execute, and press Skip step on the form.
steps.see: The plan reads completed and its step skipped: Skip step ends the step without creating anything.

steps.do: State Create a judge for tone. again, approve and execute, fill name with a new name and instructions with Is {{ evidence }} polite?, and press Continue plan. The form accepts it; the step does not.
steps.see: The plan reads failed and the step shows invalid input: instructions: instructions must reference at least one evaluation variable.... Judges has no row for that name. A failed plan cannot be run again: state the goal again.
steps.asset: Failed step with a readable reason
